item.title: The Money Flow as a Second Backbone
item.lead: Where the operations layer organizes human interaction, the dossier describes the payment infrastructure as the system's second backbone.

blocks.text: The source presents a chain in which payments from users, via platform or payment service layers, ultimately reach agencies, creators, and intermediary companies. The dossier primarily emphasizes the fragmentation: various entities, countries, and payment providers can be part of the same money flow.

For the reader, it is useful to distinguish three layers. The first is the consumer moment: a purchase, tip, or microtransaction. The second is the processing layer: platform, PSP, or merchant account. The third is the business layer: agency, holding, payout entity, or other recipient. The source suggests that precisely the combination of these layers can complicate visibility into the ultimate beneficiary.

The dossier also uses this to explain why individual small payments provide little analytical insight. A large number of small transactions can collectively form a significant pattern. For financial investigations, the focus therefore shifts from a single payment to frequency, timing, counterparties, and the payout route.

This PDF addresses carding and money laundering practices exclusively as descriptions of the source claim. No operational steps or instructions are provided for committing fraud. The relevant research objective is to identify money flows, responsibilities, and anomalous patterns.

blocks.label: RESEARCH PRINCIPLE
blocks.text: Follow money flows as a chain: consumer -> platform/PSP -> payout layer -> ultimate beneficiary. The dossier claim must be substantiated for each transition with primary documents.
